headline: Oil fell about 3% after Iran offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and US futures are up after Friday's tech sell-off. Expect a steady to slightly higher start, but Nifty is still stuck between 22,500 and 23,500.

mood.label: Mixed
mood.why: Dashboard Neutral (+14, 2 of 4 checks agree); FIIs still mostly bet on a fall. Overnight data as of 08:49 IST.

key_points.text: Brent crude is down **2.9%** to about $110 after Iran offered to reopen Hormuz. Cheaper oil helps India, which imports most of its oil.
US stocks fell hard on Friday (Nasdaq −2.9%), but US futures are up this morning.
FIIs bought **₹3,599 crore** of shares on Friday, a big buying day.
My call: a small continuation of Friday's rise is slightly more likely than a pullback, staying within 23,000 to 23,500. Low confidence.

sections.title: What changed overnight
sections.summary: Since Friday's close the news has mostly improved, which supports Friday's rise.

points.text: GIFT Nifty (Nifty futures traded overseas) was near **23,260**, about flat on its own Friday close, per a pre-market report.
US futures are up after Trump said the Iran war will end soon, partly reversing Friday's −1.8% S&P 500 fall. Asia is mixed.
Oil is down **2.9%**, while US bond rates (4.93%) and the dollar are flat, so there is no new pressure from rates.
US-listed Infosys (+2.9%), HDFC Bank (+1.7%) and ICICI Bank (+1.1%) rose on Friday, which is a good sign for IT and banks.

sections.title: Bounce or continuation?
sections.summary: After Friday's +0.5% day, a small continuation looks slightly more likely than a pullback, with low confidence.

points.text: For more gains: oil is falling, US futures are up and FIIs bought. Option sellers also built a floor at **23,000** (68,220 new put contracts).
Against: only 11.1% of FII index-futures bets are on a rise, and on Friday they added bets on a fall and bought protection.
The put-call ratio (bets on a fall compared with bets on a rise) jumped from 0.81 to **1.42** in a week, close to the 1.5 level the dashboard calls over-excited.
I'm wrong if Nifty closes below 23,000 or Iran attacks ships again.

sections.title: The big picture
sections.summary: The dashboard sees no clear direction: price is in a sideways range.

points.text: Bias score is **+14** (Neutral). Option chain (+0.4) and put-call ratio (+1.0) lean up, while price trend (−0.3) and futures/FII (0.0) don't.
Nifty (23,053) is above its 20-day average but below its 50-day (23,255) and 200-day (24,035) averages, so the longer trend is still down.
India VIX (the fear gauge) is 15.45, higher than 72% of the past year, but falling.

sections.title: What big investors are doing
sections.summary: FIIs bought shares but kept most of their bets on a fall.

points.text: FIIs bought ₹3,599 crore on Friday, after selling ₹944 crore on Thursday. Domestic funds sold ₹818 crore.
October was still **₹30,978 crore** of FII selling, while domestic funds bought ₹46,997 crore.
FIIs at 11.1% long are near the under-10% zone where bets on a fall have often been closed in a rush, but there is no sign of that yet.

sections.title: What the world is telling India
sections.summary: Oil is the biggest risk and it eased this morning, but high US interest rates still pull money away from India.

points.text: Even after today's fall, Brent near $110 is still up about 14% in a month.
Iran wants sanctions relief in return for reopening Hormuz, and the US says new strikes are still possible. A deal isn't done yet.
Six-month US Treasury bills pay 4.25%, above the Fed's 3.75–4.00% range, so the market expects **another rate hike**.

sections.title: Company results
sections.summary: The big weekend results were mostly strong, led by Reliance.

points.text: Reliance profit rose **33.8%** to ₹29,550 crore, filed after Friday's close. I couldn't confirm analysts' estimates.
NTPC profit rose 40.7%, Power Grid's 8.4%, and Indian Oil's nearly tripled.
Sun Pharma's profit fell **36%** because of a one-time loss, missing estimates of about ₹3,100 crore.

sections.title: What could change the picture
sections.summary: A busy week: the US election, the Iran talks, an expiry and US jobs data.

points.text: US midterm elections tomorrow. Reports say fighting with Iran could restart around the vote.
Nifty weekly expiry tomorrow, with the biggest bets sitting at 23,000 and 23,500.
US jobs data on Friday (19:00 IST). Strong numbers would make another Fed hike more likely.

levels.note: A close above 23,500 or below 22,500 would break the range the option sellers are defending.

watch.text: First reaction to Reliance's 33.8% profit jump.
ITC and Marico results; SBI tomorrow.
Any Iran or Hormuz news before the US vote.

bottom_line: The night was good for India: oil fell, US futures rose and FIIs turned buyers. But the dashboard is only Neutral (+14) and FIIs still hold mostly bets on a fall, so this looks like a range market rather than a new uptrend. My read is a steady to slightly higher day between 23,000 and 23,500, with low confidence. The main risk is Iran: new attacks around the US vote would push oil, and Indian stocks, the other way.
